headline_marked: Legendary actor [[Sir Patrick Stewart dies at 86]]
headline: Legendary actor Sir Patrick Stewart dies at 86
summary: The 'Star Trek' and 'X-Men' star passed away at his home in Los Angeles after a battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia.
details: Sir Patrick Stewart, the acclaimed actor known for his roles as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 'Star Trek' and Professor Charles Xavier in 'X-Men', has died at the age of 86.
According to a statement on his X account, Stewart passed away at his home in Los Angeles in the care of his wife, Sunny, following a journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.

Born into poverty in Yorkshire, England, Stewart found a 'safe space' in acting at age 12 after being introduced to Shakespeare. He later became a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in the 1960s.
Despite his stage success, he achieved global mainstream fame at 47 when he was cast as Captain Picard in 'Star Trek: The Next Generation', a role he continued to play into his 80s.
Stewart also became a central figure in the Marvel Cinematic Universe as the telepathic mutant Professor X in the 'X-Men' film franchise starting in 2000.
Knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth II for his contributions to drama, Stewart was revered for his discipline and his ability to bring depth to cerebral characters.
Throughout his career, he transitioned from a classically trained stage actor to a sci-fi and fantasy icon, leaving behind a massive legacy in both theatre and cinema.

headline_marked: Mystery surrounds [[death of former Air Force officer]] Tahsif Souri
headline: Mystery surrounds death of former Air Force officer Tahsif Souri
summary: The body of 28-year-old Flight Lieutenant K M Tahsif Souri was recovered from the Turag River; his father rejects suicide claims, calling for a full investigation.
details: The body of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant K M Tahsif Souri, 28, was recovered from the Turag River in the Uttara area of Dhaka. His family has expressed deep shock and rejected the possibility of suicide, with his father stating that a proper investigation will reveal the true culprits.
Tahsif had left his home in Uttara on Tuesday evening, after which he went out with a friend, Deep, on separate motorcycles. CCTV footage shows them leaving together at 6:31 PM.
His family attempted to contact him throughout the night. At 1:35 AM on Wednesday, Tahsif sent a voice message to his mother stating that he was returning home, but he never arrived.
The Naval Police recovered his body on Wednesday afternoon near the Rajabari Ghat in the North Khan area. He was identified through an iPhone found in his pocket.

While initial police reports indicated no visible signs of injury on the body, a full autopsy was conducted at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College. Samples of his stomach, liver, and kidney have been sent for lab tests to determine the exact cause of death.
Tahsif's family is concerned that his motorcycle, which he took when he was leaving home, is still missing. They have provided the details and photos of the bike to the police for the investigation.
Tahsif was the eldest of three siblings and the unmarried same son of a former Padma Oil Company director. He was buried in Uttara on Thursday after funeral prayers.
caption:
A former Air Force officer's body was found in the Turag River after he sent a final voice message to his mother at 1:35 AM.

The body of former Air Force Flight Lieutenant K M Tahsif Souri, 28, was recovered from the Turag River in the Uttara area of Dhaka. His family has expressed deep shock and rejected the possibility of suicide, with his father stating that a proper investigation will reveal the true culprits.

Tahsif had left his home in Uttara on Tuesday evening, after which he went out with a friend, Deep, on separate motorcycles. CCTV footage shows them leaving together at 6:31 PM.

His family attempted to contact him throughout the night. At 1:35 AM on Wednesday, Tahsif sent a voice message to his mother stating that he was returning home, but he never arrived.

The Naval Police recovered his body on Wednesday afternoon near the Rajabari Ghat in the North Khan area. He was identified through an iPhone found in his pocket.

While initial police reports indicated no visible signs of injury on the body, a full autopsy was conducted at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College. Samples of his stomach, liver, and kidney have been sent for lab tests to determine the exact cause of death.

Tahsif's family is concerned that his motorcycle, which he took when he was leaving home, is still missing. They have provided the details and photos of the bike to the police for the investigation.

Tahsif was the eldest of three siblings and the unmarried same son of a former Padma Oil Company director. He was buried in Uttara on Thursday after funeral prayers.
